proof_spine: An image element carries a source preimage witness; combine or invert those witnesses in the source subgroup and map the result forward.
A preimage subgroup is closed because the homomorphism transports source operations into the target subgroup.
The kernel is the preimage of the target identity and is closed under multiplication and inverse.
The range is the image of the whole source carrier, which is itself a subgroup.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm subgroup_map_closed:
    ? forall G, H nonempty_set, source &group::Group<G>, target &group::Group<H>, f fn(x G) H, S power_set(G):
        $group_homomorphism::is_group_hom(G, H, source, target, f)
        $subgroup::is_subgroup(G, source, S)
        =>:
            $subgroup::is_subgroup(H, target, \subgroup_map<G, H, f>(S))
    \subgroup_map<G, H, f>(S) = {y H: $has_subgroup_map_preimage(G, H, f, S, y)}
    witness $has_subgroup_map_preimage(G, H, f, S, target.one) from source.one
    claim:
        ? forall a, b H:
            a $in \subgroup_map<G, H, f>(S)
            b $in \subgroup_map<G, H, f>(S)
            =>:
                target.mul(a, b) $in \subgroup_map<G, H, f>(S)
        by def $has_subgroup_map_preimage(G, H, f, S, a)
        obtain x from $has_subgroup_map_preimage(G, H, f, S, a)
        by def $has_subgroup_map_preimage(G, H, f, S, b)
        obtain y from $has_subgroup_map_preimage(G, H, f, S, b)
        witness $has_subgroup_map_preimage(G, H, f, S, target.mul(a, b)) from source.mul(x, y):
            f(source.mul(x, y)) = target.mul(f(x), f(y)) = target.mul(a, b)
    claim:
        ? forall a H:
            a $in \subgroup_map<G, H, f>(S)
            =>:
                target.inv(a) $in \subgroup_map<G, H, f>(S)
        by def $has_subgroup_map_preimage(G, H, f, S, a)
        obtain x from $has_subgroup_map_preimage(G, H, f, S, a)
        release thm group_homomorphism::group_hom_map_inv(G, H, source, target, f, x)
        witness $has_subgroup_map_preimage(G, H, f, S, target.inv(a)) from source.inv(x):
            f(source.inv(x)) = target.inv(f(x)) = target.inv(a)
    by def $subgroup::is_subgroup(H, target, \subgroup_map<G, H, f>(S))
blocks.reusable_lesson: An image subgroup proof follows the preimage witnesses; group_hom_map_inv is the only nondefinitional transport needed for inverse closure.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm subgroup_comap_closed:
    ? forall G, H nonempty_set, source &group::Group<G>, target &group::Group<H>, f fn(x G) H, T power_set(H):
        $group_homomorphism::is_group_hom(G, H, source, target, f)
        $subgroup::is_subgroup(H, target, T)
        =>:
            $subgroup::is_subgroup(G, source, \subgroup_comap<G, H, f>(T))
    \subgroup_comap<G, H, f>(T) = {q G: f(q) $in T}
    f(source.one) = target.one
    target.one $in T
    f(source.one) $in T
    claim:
        ? forall x, y G:
            x $in \subgroup_comap<G, H, f>(T)
            y $in \subgroup_comap<G, H, f>(T)
            =>:
                source.mul(x, y) $in \subgroup_comap<G, H, f>(T)
        f(x) $in T
        f(y) $in T
        f(source.mul(x, y)) = target.mul(f(x), f(y))
        target.mul(f(x), f(y)) $in T
        f(source.mul(x, y)) $in T
    claim:
        ? forall x G:
            x $in \subgroup_comap<G, H, f>(T)
            =>:
                source.inv(x) $in \subgroup_comap<G, H, f>(T)
        f(x) $in T
        release thm group_homomorphism::group_hom_map_inv(G, H, source, target, f, x)
        f(source.inv(x)) = target.inv(f(x))
        target.inv(f(x)) $in T
        f(source.inv(x)) $in T
    by def $subgroup::is_subgroup(G, source, \subgroup_comap<G, H, f>(T))
blocks.reusable_lesson: Preimages are structurally simpler than images: no existential witnesses are needed, only homomorphism transport of the three subgroup operations.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm group_kernel_closed:
    ? forall G, H nonempty_set, source &group::Group<G>, target &group::Group<H>, f fn(x G) H:
        $group_homomorphism::is_group_hom(G, H, source, target, f)
        =>:
            $subgroup::is_subgroup(G, source, \group_kernel<G, H, target.one, f>)
    by def $group::group_laws(H, target.mul, target.one, target.inv)
    \group_kernel<G, H, target.one, f> = {q G: f(q) = target.one}
    f(source.one) = target.one
    claim:
        ? forall x, y G:
            x $in \group_kernel<G, H, target.one, f>
            y $in \group_kernel<G, H, target.one, f>
            =>:
                source.mul(x, y) $in \group_kernel<G, H, target.one, f>
        f(source.mul(x, y)) = target.mul(f(x), f(y)) = target.mul(target.one, target.one) = target.one
    claim:
        ? forall x G:
            x $in \group_kernel<G, H, target.one, f>
            =>:
                source.inv(x) $in \group_kernel<G, H, target.one, f>
        release thm group_homomorphism::group_hom_map_inv(G, H, source, target, f, x)
        f(source.inv(x)) = target.inv(f(x)) = target.inv(target.one)
        target.mul(target.inv(target.one), target.one) = target.one
        release thm group::mul_one(H, target.mul, target.one, target.inv, target.inv(target.one))
        target.mul(target.inv(target.one), target.one) = target.inv(target.one)
        target.inv(target.one) = target.one
        f(source.inv(x)) = target.one
    by def $subgroup::is_subgroup(G, source, \group_kernel<G, H, target.one, f>)
blocks.reusable_lesson: The only nontrivial kernel-specific step is deriving target.inv(target.one) = target.one from the group laws.
